messages:
amelia: Hey team — quick heads up, spotted a mismatch between the API and our API reference for POST /v1/generate. Docs show `max_tokens` and a single `text` field in the response, but the runtime accepts `max_new_tokens` and returns `output: [{text: ...}]`. This is causing confusion in customer reports and tests failing in the SDK examples.

raj: Ugh, that would explain the integration tests failing for the JS SDK example. Where did you see the runtime using `max_new_tokens`?

amelia: Reproduced locally against the hosted staging endpoint. curl request I used:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/fast-1","max_new_tokens":64,"prompt":"Summarize..."}'
```

response snippet: 

```
{"id":"gen_abc","output":[{"text":"Short summary...","metadata":{}}],"model":"redwood/fast-1"}
```

raj: Great repro, thanks. So docs currently show examples like: `{"max_tokens":64}` and `response.choices[0].text` — that obviously won't work.

maria: I reviewed the docs site source — the param table and example payload are in `content/api/generate.md` and the SDK snippets are auto-generated from `site/_snippets/generate_examples.yaml`. Looks like older naming (`max_tokens`) snuck back in during an earlier merge.

sam: CI already caught something: docs-bot posted a failure on the examples lint.

docs-bot: docs-ci: example-validation failed for `content/api/generate.md` (schema mismatch). See CI run: https://ci.internal.redwood/1234 :x:

linter-bot: markdown-lint: code-block style issues in `content/api/generate.md` — use fenced code blocks with language tags.

raj: Plan: I'll update the param table to mention `max_new_tokens` as the current canonical name and add a note mapping `max_tokens` -> `max_new_tokens` for backward compatibility. Amelia — can you paste the exact response schema you saw so Maria can update examples?

amelia: Pasting cleaned example below (use in docs):

```
Request:
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model":"redwood/fast-1",
  "max_new_tokens":64,
  "temperature":0.7,
  "prompt":"Explain recursion in a paragraph"
}

Response:
{
  "id":"gen_abc",
  "model":"redwood/fast-1",
  "output":[
    {"text":"Recursion is...","type":"text"}
  ]
}
```

maria: Perfect. I'll update the examples in `content/api/generate.md` and regenerate the SDK snippets under `site/_snippets`. Also will add a migration note at the top: "If you previously used `max_tokens`, rename to `max_new_tokens`; old clients may be mapped server-side but explicit rename recommended."

sam: After you push, I'll run the docs CI locally and check the snippet generator output. Also can you add a small unit test for the example validator? Saves a second CI round.

maria: Yep — adding a test that validates the example response against the response schema. Quick patch:

```
- examples: # old
-  request: {"max_tokens": 64}
+ examples: # updated
+  request: {"max_new_tokens": 64}
```

raj: Can we also ensure the Python and curl snippets use the same field name? I noticed the Python snippet uses kwargs in the SDK call: `client.generate(model="fast-1", max_tokens=64)` — that needs updating too.

maria: Good catch. I'll update the generator mapping so SDK snippet shows `max_new_tokens` in the raw HTTP example, and keep the SDK call idiomatic (for now SDK still accepts `max_tokens` but we'll add a deprecation note).

amelia: For release notes / migration guide — recommend short bullet under docs change log: "rename `max_tokens` -> `max_new_tokens` for Generate endpoints; SDKs will continue to accept `max_tokens` for one release cycle."

sam: @maria please @mention me in the PR when ready. I'll run docs-ci and then queue a small hotfix release for the examples site.

maria: Will do. Creating PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/987 — contains param table fix, updated examples, snippet regen, and a migration note. Please review.

raj: Reviewing now. Quick request: add a single integration example verifying both `max_tokens` and `max_new_tokens` accepted by server (to reassure customers).

maria: Adding that test in the PR.

amelia: Thanks all. After merge, can someone post an update in #general so support doesn't get surprised by the wording change? :eyes:

sam: I'll post the note and link to the PR after merge. :shipit:
